lessons: The May-2026 cycle correctly flagged the Digital Omnibus as provisional and told readers to confirm against the Official Journal. Three months later it was law. Any skill carrying a pending-legislation caveat needs that caveat re-tested every cycle, because the caveat itself goes stale.

iso.org is Cloudflare bot-gated to curl AND to headless Chromium, so the ISO 42001 publication date could not be re-confirmed this cycle. ISO/IEC 42005 and 42006 are reported published in 2025 but were not verifiable for the same reason and are deliberately NOT stated in the skill. Try an institutional or IEC-webstore route next cycle.
lexology.com hard-403s, so the February 2026 PPA consent opinion rests on a secondary analysis. Find the PPA publication on gov.il and cite that instead.

Reported but not encoded for lack of a verified source: the PPA PETs-for-AI guide (Jan 2026), PPA recommendations on AI agents (Jul 2026), the national AI plan approved 16 June 2026, the MoH February 2026 v2.0 principles for AI interventional clinical trials, and BoI Directive 369 on model risk management. Each is a real lead; source them next cycle.

EUR-Lex ELI permalinks (eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/...) return HTTP 202 with an empty body to every non-interactive fetch. The CELEX form (legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A...) renders in a browser. Use CELEX for citations.

Round-1 Judge caught a fabrication that had survived every prior cycle: the six MoI regulatory principles were three-quarters invented (whole-of-government approach, balanced and proportionate intervention, regular review and evolution do not exist in the policy), the policy title was wrong, and a day-level publication date was asserted that the PDF does not carry. All were corrected from the PDF itself. Lesson: a list that reads plausibly and is repeated in a reference file is exactly what nobody re-checks.

Round-1 Expert found classify_eu_ai_act_risk.py evaluated Article 5 prohibitions BEFORE the Article 2 scope test, so Israel-only systems were told they were Prohibited under a regulation that does not reach them. Fixed by reordering. Any classifier in this catalogue should be run against an out-of-scope input as a standing test.

Deferred Expert MAJORs: Amendment 13 numeric substance (DPO trigger thresholds, database registration thresholds, the penalty formula) is still qualitative and has no evidence entry; the sector-regulator table asserts AMAR, CMISA, MoT and MoD requirements with no sources; cross-border transfer of personal data out of Israel is not covered at all despite the checklist depending on it; there is no data-statement template despite the description promising one; and classify_eu_ai_act_risk.py has no --json output to feed generate_model_card.py.
Article 6(3) derogation is now flagged in the decision framework but not implemented as a screen in the classifier. Implement it next cycle after re-reading Article 6.

Round-2 Judge found four more unsourced assertions that had survived multiple cycles: the 31 October 2025 DPO grace-period expiry (asserted in four files, no source anywhere), 'April 2025' as the PPA draft AI guidance publication month (both cited sources are dated May 2025), an 'endorsed 1 August 2025 via adequacy decisions' framing of the GPAI Code (the Commission page says only that it was published 10 July 2025 and confirmed as an adequate voluntary tool), and an invented 'Risk Management Toolbox' and 'National AI Ethics Committee' attributed to the AI Policy Coordination Center. All were softened or deleted. The pattern is precise-looking dates attached to real events; they are the least likely thing anyone re-checks.

Round-2 Expert found the classifier's Article 5 screen had narrowed 5(1)(c) social scoring to public authorities (the statute covers any actor) and omitted 5(1)(a) and 5(1)(g), while its caveat said the only gap was the Omnibus additions, turning an incomplete screen into an affirmative clearance. Also: --input mode defaulted every absent or misspelled key to false, so a typo'd JSON returned a confident Minimal-risk. Both fixed; the script now validates every key and rejects unknown ones. Standing test for any classifier in this catalogue: run it with an empty input, a typo'd key, and an out-of-scope input.

The Hebrew file was missing the entire EU AI Act risk-tier obligations table, including the prohibited tier, while the English carried it. Heading counts matched, so no structural gate caught it. Compare TABLES between the two languages, not just headings.
